faq.title: Common questions, [answered.]
faq.description: Everything you need to know about earnings, dividends, and how they can affect your CFD positions.

items.q: What affects stock and index CFDs around earnings dates?
items.a: Earnings releases can increase volatility, spread changes, and margin requirements on related CFDs.

items.q: What is an ex-dividend date in CFD trading?
items.a: It is the date when dividend adjustment is applied based on your open position direction.

items.q: Do long and short positions get treated differently?
items.a: Yes. Long positions are generally credited while short positions are generally charged for dividend adjustments.

items.q: Why should I check the earnings calendar before trading?
items.a: It helps you plan exposure, avoid surprises, and prepare for potential margin and volatility shifts.

items.q: Can one event impact multiple instruments?
items.a: Yes. A single corporate event may affect several related index or stock CFDs.

items.q: How can I reduce risk during high-margin periods?
items.a: Use smaller position sizes, monitor free margin, and keep a risk buffer before major events.

items.q: Where can I get help if I’m unsure?
items.a: Contact support before market close for guidance on instrument details and margin impact.

items.question: What is an Economic Calendar?
items.answer: An economic data calendar is a schedule of upcoming economic events and data releases, such as interest rate decisions, GDP figures, employment reports, and inflation data, that can influence financial markets. Traders use it to plan positions ahead of high-impact events.

items.question: How do I use the Economic Calendar to trade?
items.answer: Filter upcoming economic events by date range, impact level (High / Medium / Low), and country. Before a high-impact release, check the forecast vs. previous values. If the actual data is available, compare it with the forecast to understand how the market may react. Always use proper risk management around new events.

items.question: What does the impact level (High / Medium / Low) mean?
items.answer: Impact levels indicate how much a data release has historically influenced financial markets. High-impact events — such as Non-Farm Payrolls, FOMC decisions, and CPI releases — can cause significant market volatility. Medium-impact events may cause moderate price movements, while low-impact events generally have a more limited effect on market prices.

items.question: What time zone does the calendar use?
items.answer: By default, the economic calendar displays event times in your local time zone. You can switch to UTC or another time zone using the selector at the top of the calendar, making it easier to track economic events across different markets.

items.question: Is the Economic Calendar data real-time?
items.answer: Yes. The real-time economic calendar updates actual values as soon as official data is released. Forecast and previous figures are sourced from leading financial data providers and updated regularly.
